heroHeading: Women, building the skills to defend the internet.
heroBody: WiCyS SRMIST is a student community where women dig into cybersecurity together — breaking things in the lab, defending them in CTFs, and building the network to take it professional.
offeringsHeading: What a semester with us looks like

offerings.title: Workshops & labs
offerings.body: Hands-on sessions on web security, networking, cryptography, and tooling — no prior experience assumed.

offerings.title: Capture the Flag
offerings.body: Weekly practice and travel teams for national and global CTFs, with writeups reviewed together afterwards.

offerings.title: Speaker sessions
offerings.body: Practitioners from SOCs, red teams, and product security talk about the work and how they got there.

offerings.title: Mentorship circles
offerings.body: Small groups pairing newer members with seniors and alumni for guidance on skills, internships, and interviews.

heading: About the chapter
intro: Women in Cybersecurity (WiCyS) is the global organization working on the recruitment, retention, and advancement of women in the field. Our SRMIST student chapter brings that work to campus — a group of students learning security together and building the network to carry it into careers.

children.text: Build a durable community of women in cybersecurity at SRMIST by providing training, mentorship, and a way in. We think a more representative security workforce is a stronger one — for the people in it and for everyone it protects.

Women hold under a quarter of cybersecurity roles worldwide, and the gap starts early — often before the first internship. The chapter is one answer: a supportive place to get technical, get connected, and stay in the field.

values.def: A place where women and allies can ask the basic question, share the half-finished project, and find someone who has been there.
Workshops, CTFs, and labs that put hands on keyboards. Theory matters, but it sticks when you have broken something with it.
Every session is free and open to any SRMIST student. We meet people where they are instead of assuming a starting point.
Members run the events, lead the teams, and represent the chapter externally — the resume line is a side effect of the real thing.
